objections.claim_attacked: hypothesis: default 30 congestion iterations were also insufficient
objections.objection: The record supports that the configuration at layer adjustment 0.45 with default 30 iterations failed GRT, and that a later configuration at 0.2 with 35 iterations was reported to complete. Because both variables changed together and the iteration sweep results are not itemized, the record does not show that 30 was insufficient independent of the layer adjustment, nor that 35 was necessary. Correct version: call the final change a two-parameter workaround reported to complete GRT; treat necessity and sufficiency of each parameter as not-determinable-from-this-record.

objections.claim_attacked: chosen_intervention attaches both parameter changes to direct_quote
objections.objection: The stored direct_quote.text contains only the routing-layer-adjustment clause; the congestion-iteration count of 35 appears in chosen_intervention prose but not in the dated quoted text. The quote therefore proves attribution for 0.45 to 0.2 only; the 35-iteration part needs the same verbatim support or an explicit disclosed ellipsis/locator.

As a single resolution number this overstates the evidence. It mixes a fairly specific observed failure and named-participant report with an unmeasured post_state, no PR or merge statement, and an automatic not_planned/Stale closure in 2026. Correct calibration: high confidence that the failure and reported workaround statement exist in the record, much lower confidence that the change was merged, generalizable, or root-caused.

mechanism_check: The supported causal chain is minimal and correlational: low placement density coexisted with a congestion hotspot near the top/macro and a failed GRT at adjustment 0.45 with 30 iterations; eder-matheus then reported changing layer adjustment to 0.2 and congestion iterations to 35, after which GRT was said to finish. It is plausible that routing/tuning changes altered congestion handling enough for completion, but the record does not define the high-versus-low adjustment semantics and does not show which change mattered. The macro-looping path around the macro remains a separate suspected cause deferred to issue #5971, so root cause is not established by this incident record.
evidence_check: post_state is asserted, not measured. What is actually reported is only that GRT/BoomTile could finish or complete after the parameter changes. A closed-out fix would still have to show a post-run DRC or overflow count, runtime, exact final parameter set, tool/flow versions, log or transcript reference, PR/commit/config-merge evidence, and confirmation of whether the suspected #5971 macro-loop behavior disappeared. The 2026 not_planned/Stale automatic closure is not validating evidence.
attribution_check: direct_quote is attributed to a named participant, eder-matheus, with date 2024-11-14 and locator equal to the issue URL, and it does support the narrow claim that the layer adjustment was changed from 0.45 to 0.2. It does not, as stored, include the separate clause that congestion iterations were changed to 35; that part is not-determinable-from-this-record as a verbatim quote unless the omitted material is intended and explicitly disclosed.
missing_from_story: Definition and direction of set-global-routing-layer-adjustment: what a higher or lower numeric adjustment does to effective routing supply in this flow.
Whether 0.2 with 30 iterations or 0.45 with 35 iterations was run separately, and the outcomes of each isolated change.
Itemized sweep results for the overflow/congestion iteration count beyond the default 30.
Exact meaning of the 20k figure: GRT overflow, congestion DRC markers, GUI-reported violations, or detailed-route DRCs.
Macro identity/location and whether the hotspot was tied to macro halo, keepout, blockage, pin access, or the suspected looping path deferred to #5971.
Post-fix measurements: residual overflow/DRCs, runtime, final routed state, and whether the result reproduced across runs or seeds.
Whether the parameter change became a code, default, script, or ORFS config change, with PR/commit reference.
Why the issue was closed as not_planned/Stale despite the reported completion, and whether #5971 was later confirmed as the real root cause.
Impact on the other asap7 designs from which the original 0.45 adjustment was derived.
most_defensible_part: The narrow direct_quote attribution for the layer-adjustment statement: eder-matheus, dated 2024-11-14, located at issue #6066, supporting only the claim that routing layer adjustment was changed from 0.45 to 0.2 in the reported GRT completion.
